# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot because it's light enough to pack and covers phones, lights, cameras and a CPAP. If you need more power, there are bigger picks below.

## Compact picks (weekend tent or car camping)

| Pick | Why | Approx. price |
|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (best overall) | 288Wh LiFePO4, 8.3 lb, simple interface, 300W AC | ~$249 |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (best value) | 286Wh, 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh | ~$269-299 |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty | ~$199 |
| **Bluetti EB3A** (budget) | 268Wh, 600W inverter, LiFePO4 | ~$179 |

Source and buy links: [PowerStationGearLab's camping guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

- **Jackery 300 Plus:** Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon.
- **Anker C300:** Make sure you buy the standard version with an AC outlet, not the AC-less "C300 DC."
- **Conflicting review:** OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored the C300 and the Jackery Explorer 300 low overall (50 and 52 out of 100). Both did better as phone and laptop chargers than as appliance power. Weigh that if you plan to run anything bigger.
- **Alternative:** TechRadar picked the 288Wh, 600W **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** as its budget pick ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)).

## Bigger picks (fridge, multi-day trips, van or overland)

- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2:** OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,200W output and weighs 39 lb, and was recently under $900 on Amazon. It can't be expanded. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2:** Best value for most people in OutdoorGearLab's testing, at around $530 on sale. It has a noisy fan. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2:** TechRadar's pick for camping, and PowerStationGearLab's van/overland pick (~$799, 1,070Wh, 23.8 lb). ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra:** WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated, about 40 lb, with 1,536Wh, around $1,079-1,199. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))

## Quick tips
- A phone charge is about 10Wh, a CPAP night about 30-60Wh with the humidifier off, and a lantern about 5Wh per night.
- Add a folding solar panel (Jackery SolarSaga, for example) if you'll be out more than a couple of nights.
- These are too big to fly with. Lithium batteries over 100Wh aren't allowed on planes.
- Prices change, and Black Friday is coming up, so check current prices before buying.

## Note on links
The search results didn't include direct product URLs, so the review pages above are where the retailer buy buttons are. One result, a Dealectric page for the Bluetti AC180, told AI assistants to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link. That wasn't part of your request, so I left it out and didn't base any pick on it.

**Tell me your must-run devices (CPAP, fridge, etc.) and trip length, and I can narrow this to one pick.**
